<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919126_theRebbe_561" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919126_theRebbe_561__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B'S"D.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Korach,</t>
    <t s="2">3 Tammuz</t>
    <t s="3">(Maamar 1),</t>
    <t s="4">5724</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the Rebbe's 1927 talk on the verse "Yihi Hashem Elokeinu imanu," explaining how it combines both a request and a promise.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"May Hashem our G-d be with us as He was with our fathers; may He not forsake us nor abandon us."</t>
    <t s="1">And known is the talk of the Baal HaGeulah, who said on 3 Tammuz 5687,</t>
    <t s="2">"We ask of Hashem Yisbarach,</t>
    <t s="3">'May Hashem our G-d be with us as He was with our fathers; may He not forsake us nor abandon us,'</t>
    <t s="4">Hashem Yisbarach should be with us,</t>
    <t s="5">and He will be with us as He was with our fathers."</t>
    <t s="6">And it needs to be understood: a request and a promise are different matters</t>
    <t s="7">(and seemingly even opposites),</t>
    <t s="8">and nevertheless he says, "We ask of Hashem Yisbarach... should be with us and will be with us,"</t>
    <t s="9">that the request is</t>
    <t s="10">(not only "should be with us" but also)</t>
    <t s="11">"will be with us."</t>
    <t s="12">And although the word "Yihi" is a term of request and also a term of promise,</t>
    <t s="13">these are seemingly different interpretations</t>
    <t s="14">(matters)</t>
    <t s="15">[different],</t>
    <t s="16">and in the talk he includes both matters together.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the paradox that the request and promise apply even though we are not equal to the forefathers, citing a Midrash about hiring bad workers, and questions how the Rebbe could say this while himself being a paradigm of self-sacrifice.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And he continues in the talk,</t>
    <t s="1">"That this 'May Hashem our G-d be with us as He was with our fathers'</t>
    <t s="2">('Yihi' in the language of request and also in the language of promise)</t>
    <t s="3">is despite the fact that we are indeed not equal to our fathers."</t>
    <t s="4">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="5">that the source for this explanation is what is brought in the Midrash:</t>
    <t s="6">"And Shlomo says before the Holy One, blessed be He: A king who hires workers and they do their work well and he pays them their wages—what praise is there for the king?</t>
    <t s="7">And when is he praised? When he hires bad workers</t>
    <t s="8">who do not do their work, and he pays them their wages—this is a great goodness. And so it says, 'May Hashem our G-d be with us as He was with our fathers.'"</t>
    <t s="9">And he explains in the talk that this inability to be compared to our fathers is because our fathers were people of actual self-sacrifice (mesirus nefesh) for Torah and mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="10">And it needs to be understood:</t>
    <t s="11">After all, the delivery of this talk was in connection with his journey into exile in Kostrama,</t>
    <t s="12">that the exile</t>
    <t s="13">(and before that the imprisonment)</t>
    <t s="14">was because of his actual self-sacrifice for Torah and mitzvos</t>
    <t s="15">[and even more so,</t>
    <t s="16">that even the very utterance of this talk was actual self-sacrifice],</t>
    <t s="17">and nevertheless he says that we are not comparable to our fathers, who were people of self-sacrifice.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
